newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini sees possible EMU launch delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini sees possible EMU launch delay.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini believes the January 1999 launch for Europe's single currency could be put back by up to six months to allow more countries to join, a senior ministry official said on Thursday.

The official was responding to queries about an interview in La Repubblica newspaper which quoted Dini as saying he believed European leaders would make a "collective assessment to decide whether it is convenient to put the start date back slightly."

Dini told the newspaper that a delay would allow the 1998 economic data of aspirant countries to be taken into account in assessing whether they meet the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU), rather than 1997 accounts alone.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said the article reflected Dini's view that "it would not be a drama if they put the EMU start...to June or July 1999".
"If this would mean more countries being in EMU, a larger EMU, this would be worthwhile," the official said.

Dini told La Repubblica he did not expect the criteria for membership would be softened. "I'm not hoping for a discount, that would be a baseless hope," he said. But he said not only Italy was having to make a huge effort to get its 1997 figures in order. "The French have their problems as well," he said.
